_readme: The font library: every typeface the edit may set words in. A caption look, a layer style and a platform-UI style name a font by its `id` here — never a CSS stack. All open licence (SIL OFL 1.1 or Apache 2.0), all from Google Fonts. `bundled: true` means HyperFrames already carries the font inside its renderer (it renders the same everywhere with nothing to fetch). Everything else must be a LOCAL file for the render to be the same every time: `python3 machine/fonts.py` lists what it would fetch (nothing is downloaded until someone runs `install`); until a font is fetched the edit draws its `fallback` font and the gate WARNS by name. Weights are the real cuts that exist — asking for another weight gets a fake one. Only the owner signs a row approved.

fonts.name: TikTok Sans
fonts.what: The typeface TikTok's own app uses. Captions set in it read as native to the feed — like the creator typed them in the app.
fonts.when_to_use: Native-looking captions and text stickers for anything that should feel made in TikTok, not by an agency.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.what: A plain, very legible screen font. Reads like a phone's own interface text.
fonts.when_to_use: Comment bubbles, DMs, search bars, lower-third titles, disclaimers — anything imitating an app screen. The fallback for every sans font not yet fetched.

fonts.name: Montserrat
fonts.what: Wide geometric capitals; at 900 it is the classic bold short-form caption.
fonts.when_to_use: Bold word-by-word captions, cards and end-card offers. What the old 'Arial Black' stack was really rendering as.

fonts.name: Poppins
fonts.what: Round, friendly geometric sans. Softer than Montserrat.
fonts.when_to_use: Captions for a warm, lifestyle or beauty read; sentence-case captions on a plate.

fonts.name: Anton
fonts.what: Tall, tight, heavy condensed capitals — a poster shout. One weight only (it is already heavy).
fonts.when_to_use: Hooks and one-word punches where the words must be huge but short on width.

fonts.name: Bebas Neue
fonts.what: Clean condensed all-caps. HyperFrames quietly swaps the name for League Gothic unless the real file is fetched.
fonts.when_to_use: Headlines and labels that need a tidy, modern condensed look; before/after labels.

fonts.name: League Gothic
fonts.what: A narrow, tall old-poster gothic. One weight only.
fonts.when_to_use: The fallback for Anton and Bebas Neue until they are fetched; tall stacked headlines.

fonts.name: Archivo Black
fonts.what: A dense, blocky heavy sans — punchy without being condensed. One weight only.
fonts.when_to_use: Hooks and card text that should hit hard and still read at a glance.

fonts.name: Roboto
fonts.what: Android's system font. Reads like a Google or YouTube screen.
fonts.when_to_use: YouTube comments, Google-style search bars, anything imitating an Android screen.

fonts.name: Roboto Condensed
fonts.what: Roboto squeezed narrow — lots of words across a line without shrinking.
fonts.when_to_use: Longer card lines, stat labels, a price row that has to fit.

fonts.name: Oswald
fonts.what: A sturdy condensed sans, a little old-newspaper.
fonts.when_to_use: The fallback for Roboto Condensed; stat cards and labels.

fonts.name: DM Sans
fonts.what: A calm, modern low-contrast sans — reads premium and quiet.
fonts.when_to_use: Clean-lower captions, cards and end cards for a premium or clinical read.

fonts.name: Playfair Display
fonts.what: A high-contrast editorial serif — magazine cover, not app.
fonts.when_to_use: An editorial or 'as seen in' moment, a quote, a luxury end card. Sparingly.

fonts.name: Caveat
fonts.what: Quick, natural handwriting — a note scribbled with a pen.
fonts.when_to_use: A handwritten label on an arrow, a 'me after 3 weeks' note, a scribbled aside.

fonts.name: Permanent Marker
fonts.when_to_use: A hand-drawn 'NEW' or price scrawl, a marker label on a before/after.
